clue.text: Signalling system delivered by horse trained to carry chart to Europe

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the chart within them
a horse that has been trained has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a chart is a map

explanation.surface: A signalling network whose messages arrive on horseback, the rider bringing a chart over to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' is the anagram signal giving SEHOR, and 'to carry' means it holds the chart; 'delivered by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a method of sending messages with flags or arms held in set positions, a visual signalling code.

clue.text: Southern European leaving station returning for trophy

indicators.note: returning means the shortened word is read backwards
one thing leaving another means it is dropped from that word

parts.note: a station is one's place or position in life

explanation.surface: A southern European walks off the station platform and heads back for a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops E from PLACE to leave PLAC, which 'returning' turns into CALP.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors once took the skin of a defeated enemy's head as a trophy, and the word now means any prize won from a rival.

clue.text: Criminal homes in on illicit booze

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook zeroes in on a stash of bootleg liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges the nine letters of HOMES IN ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits distilled illegally, traditionally by moonlight to avoid detection, are called by this name.

clue.text: Animal in minaret forced into cage

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the cage

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure or cage for animals

indicators.note: forced means pushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature found in a mosque tower is driven into a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' is the anagram signal, giving INEMART; 'into' places it within the cage, and 'in' before it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a weasel-family mammal with a bushy tail that lives in conifer forests across Europe.

clue.text: Problem after soggy food given to old retarded animal

indicators.note: after means the problem comes later than the food in the word
retarded means held back, so the pair of pieces is read from the back

parts.note: a sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An aged, slow creature is fed mush and then gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retarded' (held back) is an unusual reversal signal, giving OPOS; 'after' sets the problem last.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an American marsupial known for playing dead when threatened, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Ruler's letter to crowd

parts.note: em is the name of the letter M
a press is a crowd or throng of people

explanation.surface: A monarch's letter is handed out to the throng.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler's' reads as 'Ruler is', the 's linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who reigns over an empire is a sovereign, and so a ruler.

clue.text: Worry amongst gangs today

indicators.note: amongst means the word sits among the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Anxiety about the street gangs of the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amongst' points to the letters running across GANGS TODAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of anxiety or dread, the noun sense of worry.

clue.text: Greek hero in first part of Aeneid listened to sailors

indicators.note: the first part of the word is its opening letter
listened to means we use how the word sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: jacks, as in jack tars, are sailors

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior, in the opening book of Virgil's epic, hears the seamen out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listened to' gives JAX, which sounds like JACKS, sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty Greek warrior who fought at Troy in the Iliad.

clue.text: Government stock in favour

parts.note: stock means lineage or descent, as does race

explanation.surface: Government bonds are popular at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government stock' looks like gilts; the words are taken one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in someone's good graces means being in their favour; grace is goodwill or approval.

clue.text: Precious safe pinched by tramp

indicators.note: pinched by means held tight within another word

parts.note: to tramp is to tread heavily
safe means sure, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: A valuable safe is stolen by a vagrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' and 'tramp' look like nouns, a strongbox and a vagrant, but they are an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held very dear is cherished, so precious and this word are synonyms.

clue.text: Victoria's last daughter given gold and navy dress

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's youngest daughter wore a gown of gold and navy blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a verb here, to decorate, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate or embellish something is to adorn it, as one dresses a window or a shop.

clue.text: Change not starting with article on time in care facility

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to morph is to change form
an is the indefinite article
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter something not at the outset, involving a paper on time spent in a nursing home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops M from MORPH to leave ORPH.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution that houses and looks after children without parents is a home providing care.

clue.text: Mail handler tore stamps apart

indicators.note: apart means torn into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A post office worker rips stamps to shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' rearranges the letters of TORE STAMPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of a post office deals with the letters and parcels passing through it.

clue.text: Boats heading off to fish

indicators.note: heading off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: keel is a poetic word for a ship or boat

explanation.surface: Vessels set off on a fishing trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes K from KEELS; keel for a boat is a literary usage.
explanation.definitionFit: These are long snake-like fish, eaten jellied in East London.

clue.text: Old flour ground in shed is resistant to the elements

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the shed

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: flour is ground, and ground here means milled into a new arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: Old flour milled in an outbuilding stands up to the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the anagram signal giving OLOURF, and 'in' places it within; 'shed' is a verb, to cast off, not the outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric dyed so its colour does not run or fade in washing or sunlight withstands such exposure.

clue.text: Quip about animal eating companion in farmyard?

indicators.note: eating means the reversed animal takes the companion inside
about means the animal is turned round

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a pig is a fellow animal that might keep a horse company in a farmyard

explanation.surface: A joke about a beast that gobbles up its barnyard friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives ERAM and 'eating' wraps it round the companion. The animal is a female horse, not the male sheep many solvers first reach for.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, witty saying, so a quip is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Dear old flame and VIP seen dancing

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, an old flame

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A former lover and a celebrity are spotted on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges VIP SEEN into PENSIVE; 'Dear' is about price, not affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly means high-priced, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Manuscript back with different cover

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: different means other

explanation.surface: A manuscript returned with a new binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MS into SM.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it thickly, as a cake smothered in cream.

clue.text: Photo doctored to rubbish manifesto's last controversial topic

indicators.note: a doctored photo has been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A faked photograph is used to trash the end of a party's manifesto on a divisive issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctored' is the anagram signal, giving HOTPO; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue too sensitive for anyone to want to handle is a contentious matter, so the idiom fits.

clue.text: Trump losing papers here?

indicators.note: losing means the papers are dropped from the word

parts.note: Donald Trump was the US president
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Is this where Donald Trump mislaid his documents?
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes ID from PRESIDENT; the question mark flags 'here' as an unusual definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is here is in attendance, as in answering a roll call.

clue.text: Time to put out chocolate?

parts.note: to put someone out is to ruffle or upset them

explanation.surface: Is it time to bring out the chocolates?
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' means upset, not set out on a plate; the question mark marks a chocolate as one kind among many.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is a soft round chocolate sweet, an example of the confection.

clue.text: Took pint to stop row with editor

indicators.note: to stop means to come at the end, so the pint follows the row

parts.note: ado is fuss or a row

explanation.surface: Someone drank a pint to end an argument with the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took' is in the sense of taking on a child or an idea as one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a child, a plan or a name is to take it as one's own.

clue.text: Question a new civil engineer suspiciously

parts.note: to question is to ask

explanation.surface: Interrogate a newly qualified engineer with distrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at someone this way is with doubt or distrust, usually sidelong.

clue.text: Kind of dessert served at end of luncheon

indicators.note: served at means the dessert is placed after the letter
the end of the word is its final letter

parts.note: an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A sort of pudding brought out as the lunch finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of dessert' looks like one phrase, but 'Kind' alone is the definition, meaning pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and this word both describe someone pleasant and good-natured.

clue.text: Fire reported in water slide

indicators.note: reported means the word as heard, not as written

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: A blaze is reported at the water park's slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' is the verb to shoot, not a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a sloping channel, and at a pool one carries people down into the water.

clue.text: Attractive man married to queen crashed in squat

parts.note: a hunk is an attractive, muscular man
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a crashed computer is down

explanation.surface: A handsome man weds royalty, then crashes in a squat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squat' is a verb, to crouch, not an occupied building.
explanation.definitionFit: To crouch low or settle in for the long haul is to squat.

clue.text: Push tip of dart into weapon turned on Europe

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the weapon
turned means the weapon is read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: the tip of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Drive a dart's point into a gun aimed at the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes NUG from GUN, and 'into' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle push, especially with the elbow.

clue.text: Swimmer in ocean race crossing Atlantic to start with

indicators.note: to start with means the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A competitor in a transatlantic ocean swimming race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like a human racer but is a killer whale.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a marine mammal, so a swimmer in the sea.

clue.text: Brief up on new medicine

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Get up to speed on a new drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of BRIEF UP ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling and anti-inflammatory drug.

clue.text: Weak sides leaving embarrassing 17

indicators.note: leaving means those letters are removed

parts.note: an embarrassing situation is awkward

indicators.note: the sides of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Feeble edges departing from an uncomfortable gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' gives W and K, the outer letters of 'Weak', which 'leaving' removes from AWKWARD. '17' points to 17-across as the definition, in its sense of a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Clue 17 means a gift, and an award is something given, a prize bestowed on someone.

clue.text: People in A&E returned to get liquid injected

indicators.note: returned means the whole is read backwards
in means the people go inside the letters

parts.note: A&E is the hospital accident and emergency department, written here as its letters
men are people

explanation.surface: Patients in casualty sent back to receive a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives AMENE, which 'returned' reverses. A&E is the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is fluid injected into the rectum, usually to clear the bowels.

clue.text: Conductor chosen by staff close to Birtwistle

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: the close of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A conductor picked by orchestra staff, almost Birtwistle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a musician, and Harrison Birtwistle was an English composer, but it is the electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which electricity enters or leaves a cell or circuit.
